experiments.description: LoRA-XS pivot: frozen A/B from SVD, train only R (24x24). 5 conditions: corpus+optimized, corpus+random, structure-only, LoRA-XS baseline, standard LoRA.
experiments.notes: NEGATIVE RESULT. All 5 conditions complete. D (LoRA-XS baseline, R≈0) = 0.4124 BEATS all corpus-initialized variants: A (corpus+optimized) = 0.4262, B (corpus+random) = 0.4268, C (structure-only) = 0.4257. Near-identity R init (corpus values on diagonal ≈ I) hurts by +3.2% vs near-zero R init. Published LoRA-XS approach correct. E (standard LoRA, 101x params) = 0.3729 wins on quality. Corpus values provide zero benefit for R initialization — near-identity perturbation reconstructs top-24 SVD components, making optimization harder than starting from scratch.
